title: The Truth About Plitvička Jezera Hotels
metaDescription: Learn why official park hotels fall short and which Plitvička Jezera entrances actually offer the best access to the lakes before booking your stay.
content:
## Myth 1: Entrance 1 (Rastovača) is the ultimate place to stay

Many booking platforms highlight Entrance 1 as the top location because it sits right next to the famous Lower Lakes and the Big Waterfall (Veliki Slap). The reality is that the Rastovača village area immediately surrounding Entrance 1 absorbs the heaviest volume of daily tour bus traffic. Accommodation here consists mostly of basic private rooms along the busy D1 highway. You will deal with highway noise and massive crowds forming at the entry gates from 8:00 AM onwards. 

## Myth 2: The official hotels at Entrance 2 offer premium resorts

Entrance 2 features the three official, state-run park hotels: Hotel Jezero, Hotel Plitvice, and Hotel Bellevue. Because they are located directly inside the park boundaries, visitors expect premium, modern facilities to match the €150 to €250 per night price tags. In reality, these properties are heavily dated, reflecting 1970s Yugoslav-era architecture and basic room standards. Skip the official state-run hotels at Entrance 2 unless you specifically need a five-minute walk to the boat dock at 7:00 AM. You are paying strictly for geographic proximity, not comfort or modern amenities.

## Myth 3: Plitvica Selo is the most convenient village

Plitvica Selo is located directly next to Entrance 3 (the P3 boat station on Lake Kozjak). Maps show it sitting right on the edge of the water. However, most travelers overestimate the convenience of staying in Plitvica Selo. Because it sits on the opposite side of the canyon from the main D1 highway, reaching it by car requires a 20-kilometer drive around the perimeter of the park via narrow, winding roads. If you do not have a rental car, getting to this village with luggage is a logistical nightmare, as the main bus stops are at Entrances 1 and 2.

## Myth 4: You need an expensive lodge for amenities

Visitors often assume they must book high-end lodges to find food and basic supplies within walking distance of the lakes. Mukinje, a small residential village located a 15-minute walk (1.5 kilometers) south of Entrance 2, proves this wrong. It offers a clear pedestrian path through the woods directly to the park entry. More importantly, Mukinje houses the only standard supermarket (Studenac) in the immediate park area, alongside a local bistro and a ski lift operational in winter. Guesthouses here typically charge €60 to €100 per night, offering better value and easier access to basic supplies than the official park hotels.


When choosing where to stay within Plitvička Jezera, prioritize logistics over scenery. No hotel offers views of the famous waterfalls from the rooms. Your primary concern should be how you plan to arrive. If arriving by public bus, staying in Mukinje or directly at Entrance 2 is required, as dragging luggage along the D1 highway to Rastovača or paying for an expensive local taxi to Plitvica Selo wastes time and money. If you have a car, Plitvica Selo offers excellent boutique guesthouses, provided you are prepared for the rural drive to reach them.

faq.question: But isn't staying at Entrance 1 required to see the Big Waterfall early?
faq.answer: No. You can easily reach the Lower Lakes and the Big Waterfall from Entrance 2 by taking the free internal park shuttle bus (ST2 to ST1), which runs every 30 minutes starting at 8:00 AM.

faq.question: But aren't the state-run hotels the only way to get multi-day park access?
faq.answer: False. While official park hotels (Jezero, Plitvice, Bellevue) will stamp a one-day ticket to extend it for a second day for free, anyone can simply purchase a standard two-day pass online in advance and stay at a cheaper private guesthouse in Mukinje.

quickAnswer: Staying right at Entrance 1 is rarely the best choice for a quiet trip. While it offers immediate access to the Lower Lakes, it is the busiest zone. Better options exist at Entrance 2 or the pedestrian-friendly village of Mukinje.
